stem: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in $8.0\text{ s}$. What distance does the car travel in this time?
markscheme: Distance = average velocity × time = ½ × 24 × 8.0 = 96 m.

help.title: What do you know?
help.text: The car starts from rest, so $u = 0$. It reaches $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ after $t = 8.0\text{ s}$, and the acceleration is uniform. You need the distance $s$.

help.title: Choose a method
help.text:
When acceleration is uniform, the **average velocity** is halfway between the start and end velocities: $\dfrac{u + v}{2}$.

Distance = average velocity × time. (This is the same as the area under a velocity–time graph.)

help.title: Find the average velocity
help.text: $\dfrac{0 + 24}{2} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Now multiply by the time.

stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Air resistance is negligible. What is the acceleration of the ball at its highest point?
options: It depends on the initial speed
markscheme: Only gravity acts on the ball at every point of its flight, so the acceleration is always $g$ downwards, even when the velocity is momentarily zero.

help.title: Which forces act?
help.text: Air resistance is negligible. At the highest point (and everywhere else in the flight), which force still acts on the ball?

help.title: Link force to acceleration
help.text: Only the ball's **weight** acts. Newton's second law says acceleration = resultant force ÷ mass, and the weight does not switch off at the top.

help.title: Velocity is not acceleration
help.text: At the top the velocity is momentarily zero, but it is **changing**, from upwards to downwards. A changing velocity means there is an acceleration.

help.title: Final answer
help.text: The acceleration is $g$ downwards at every point, including the top, so the answer is **B**.

stem: A stone is dropped from rest from a bridge $45\text{ m}$ above the water. Assume air resistance is negligible and take $g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the time taken for the stone to reach the water.

help.title: List the quantities
help.text: Dropped from rest: $u = 0$. Distance fallen $s = 45\text{ m}$, acceleration $a = g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$. You need the time $t$.

help.title: Pick an equation
help.text: You don't know the final velocity $v$, so use the equation without it: $s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2$. With $u = 0$ this becomes $s = \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the speed of the stone as it hits the water.

help.title: Choose an equation
help.text: You can use your time from (a) with $v = u + at$, or avoid it completely with $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$. Which quantities do you know?

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how air resistance would change the time taken for the stone to fall.
markscheme: Air resistance acts upwards / opposes the motion, so the resultant force (and acceleration) is less than $mg$ (less than $g$)
So the stone takes longer to fall

help.title: Direction of air resistance
help.text: The stone moves downwards. Which way does air resistance act on it?

help.title: Effect on the resultant force
help.text: Air resistance acts **upwards**, against the motion. So the resultant force is weight minus air resistance, which is less than the weight.

help.title: Effect on the motion
help.text: A smaller resultant force means a smaller acceleration (less than $g$), so the stone's speed builds up more slowly over the same 45 m.

help.title: Final answer
help.text: Air resistance opposes the motion, so the resultant force and the acceleration are less than without it. The stone therefore **takes longer** to reach the water. (One mark for each of these two points.)
